text.en: In Hiware Bazar in Maharashtra, people look after their water so well that the village is called water-positive.

Hiware Bazar in Maharashtra is a successful example of a water-positive village. Local communities took part in watershed management and rainwater harvesting.
Rainwater harvesting means collecting rainwater and letting it sink into the ground. Open soil, soak pits, ponds and trees help recharge groundwater.
The Jal Shakti Museum in New Delhi, India's first water museum, celebrates India's water heritage and inspires citizens to conserve water.
Water also changes the land: it flows, stops or curves according to the shape of the land, and the flow can in turn change the shape of the land. Rivers move towards the Arabian Sea or the Bay of Bengal.
The Luni river, which begins in the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan, is the only major Indian river that does not drain into a sea. It ends in the marshy land of the Rann of Kutch.
(additional, not in the textbook) Simple ways to save water: close taps when not in use, fix leaks, reuse water from washing vegetables for plants, and do not throw waste into ponds and rivers.
Think about how water is stored in your home, in tanks and pots, and how a dam works as a big water-storing unit.

problem.en: Name three ways to help rainwater go underground.

why.en: Roots help the soil absorb water.

prompt.en: Why is saving water important even when it rains?

requiredIdeas.en: Cement stops water from going underground

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking rain will always be enough

points.en: Communities can save water by harvesting rain.
Open soil, ponds and trees recharge groundwater.
Use water wisely and keep it clean.
